title: Empires and Isa
blurb: Persia, Greece and Rome rise. Maryam gives birth to Isa in Palestine. Christianity spreads and Rome becomes Byzantium.

events.title: Cyrus frees the captives
events.what: Cyrus of Persia takes Babylon and lets Bani Israil return to Jerusalem. His empire reaches from India to Egypt.
events.tie: Some modern scholars, like Abul Kalam Azad, identified Cyrus with Dhul-Qarnayn, the just king of Surah al-Kahf (18:83); the question remains open.

events.title: Dhul-Qarnayn's wall
events.what: A just king travels west and east, then builds an iron wall against Yajuj and Majuj. Scholars differ on who he was; some say Cyrus.

events.title: Darius builds Persepolis
events.what: Darius I rules the largest empire yet, from the Indus to Egypt, joined by royal roads. He begins the palace city of Persepolis.
events.tie: A thousand years later Persia's heartland became Muslim, giving Islam Salman al-Farisi, Sibawayh and many of its great scholars.

events.title: The temple rebuilt
events.what: Exiles back from Babylon finish rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem under Persian rule.
events.tie: Some commentators read 'Then We gave back to you a return victory' (17:6) as this restoration.
events.note: Others link 17:6 to the days of Talut and Dawud.

events.title: Buddha and Confucius
events.what: Buddha teaches in India and Confucius in China. Their ideas shape Asia for the next 2,500 years.
events.tie: The Quran names no teacher of India or China, but speaks of messengers whose stories it has not told (4:164), and scholars avoid guessing who they were.

events.title: Socrates, Plato, Aristotle
events.what: In Athens, Socrates questions everything, Plato founds his Academy, and Aristotle writes on logic, nature and ethics.
events.tie: Translated into Arabic in Abbasid Baghdad, their books shaped Muslim philosophy and the debates of al-Farabi, Ibn Sina and al-Ghazali.

events.title: Alexander conquers Persia
events.what: Alexander of Macedon defeats Persia and conquers Egypt and the east. Greek becomes the language of learning.
events.tie: Some early writers named him Dhul-Qarnayn, but scholars like Ibn Kathir rejected this, since Alexander and his teacher Aristotle worshipped idols.

events.title: Petra and the Nabataeans
events.what: Nabataean Arabs grow rich on the incense road and carve their capital, Petra, into rose-red rock.
events.tie: Their tombs at Hegra stand in al-Hijr, the land of Thamud, and their script grew into the Arabic letters of the Quran.
events.note: The Hegra tombs are Nabataean, carved many centuries after Thamud.

events.title: Ashoka's edicts
events.what: After the bloody war of Kalinga, the Maurya emperor Ashoka turns to Buddhism and carves edicts urging mercy across India.
events.tie: Islam reached Sindh in 711, and India later became home to one of the largest Muslim populations on earth.

events.title: The Tawrat in Greek
events.what: Jewish scholars in Alexandria translate their scriptures into Greek. The Septuagint becomes the Bible of the early Christians.
events.tie: The Quran says Allah sent down the Tawrat 'in which was guidance and light' (5:44).

events.title: Qin unifies China
events.what: The king of Qin conquers his rivals and becomes China's first emperor, unifying its writing, weights and roads.
events.tie: Muslims often quote 'Seek knowledge even in China', but scholars grade that saying weak.
events.note: Reported by al-Bayhaqi and others; graded weak, and by some fabricated.

events.title: The Great Wall
events.what: Qin Shi Huang links older walls into one long barrier against the steppe nomads. Later dynasties rebuild it many times.
events.tie: Some ask if it is Dhul-Qarnayn's barrier against Yajuj and Majuj, but that was iron and copper between two mountains (18:94-97).
events.note: Most scholars reject the link. The wall standing today is mostly Ming, from the 1500s.

events.title: The Maccabees
events.what: A Greek king bans Jewish worship and defiles the temple. The Maccabee family revolts and rededicates it, as Hanukkah remembers.
events.tie: The Quran says that if Allah did not check some people by others, synagogues, churches and mosques would be pulled down (22:40).

events.title: The Silk Road opens
events.what: The Han envoy Zhang Qian reaches Central Asia. Soon caravans link China with Persia and Rome.
events.tie: Muslim merchants later carried Islam along these roads to Bukhara, Samarkand and China.

events.title: Caesar's calendar
events.what: Julius Caesar sets a solar calendar of 365 days with a leap year. A year later he is murdered in the Senate.
events.tie: Islam kept the moon's twelve months (9:36), so Ramadan moves through every season.

events.title: Rome becomes an empire
events.what: Augustus becomes the first Roman emperor. Rome rules the whole Mediterranean, including Palestine and Egypt.
events.tie: Isa was born in Roman-ruled Palestine in the reign of Augustus; the Quran tells of his birth to Maryam beneath a palm tree (19:23-25).

events.title: Maryam in the temple
events.what: Maryam is dedicated to the temple before birth. Zakariya cares for her and finds her given fruit out of season.

events.title: Herod's temple
events.what: King Herod rebuilds the temple on a vast stone platform. This is the temple of Zakariya, Maryam and Yahya's time.
events.tie: Its platform holds today's al-Aqsa sanctuary, goal of the Prophet's ﷺ night journey (17:1).

events.title: Yahya is born
events.what: Old and childless, Zakariya is given Yahya, a prophet from childhood, gentle and pure.

events.title: The angels speak to Maryam
events.what: The angels tell Maryam that Allah has chosen her above the women of the worlds. Then Jibril comes to her in the form of a man, with news of a son.

events.title: The birth of Isa
events.what: Isa is born to Maryam without a father. He speaks in the cradle to defend his mother.

events.title: The killing of Yahya
events.what: Yahya condemns a ruler's unlawful marriage and is killed on the orders of Herod Antipas. Tradition keeps his head in a shrine in the Umayyad Mosque of Damascus.
events.note: His killing is told by historians and the Gospels, not the Quran, which blesses 'the day he dies' (19:15).

events.title: The miracles of Isa
events.what: Isa receives the Injil, heals the blind and the leper, raises the dead by Allah's leave, and gathers his disciples.

events.title: The disciples answer
events.what: Isa asks, 'Who are my supporters for Allah?' The disciples answer that they are Allah's supporters, and ask him to bear witness that they are Muslims.

events.title: The table from heaven
events.what: The disciples ask for a table of food from heaven. Isa prays and it is sent down as a sign.

events.title: Isa raised up
events.what: A plot to crucify Isa fails. He is not killed; Allah raises him to Himself.

events.title: The man who came running
events.what: Two messengers, then a third, come to a town and are rejected. A man runs from the far end of the city to defend them and is killed. He is told: 'Enter Paradise.'
events.note: Many commentators name the town Antioch and the man Habib the carpenter. Ibn Kathir doubted this; the Quran names neither.

events.title: The temple destroyed
events.what: Rome crushes a Jewish revolt and destroys the second temple. Bani Israil are scattered.
events.tie: Many commentators read the second punishment in Surah al-Isra, when enemies would 'enter the temple' (17:7), as this Roman destruction.

events.title: The Gospels are written
events.what: Followers of Isa write the four Gospels in Greek, decades after him. Other gospels are written too, and later set aside by the church.
events.tie: The Quran says Allah gave Isa the Injil itself (5:46); Muslims see the Gospels as later human accounts about him.

events.title: Jewish tribes in Yathrib
events.what: As Rome crushes Jewish revolts, Arab historians say Jewish clans settle in the oasis of Yathrib, awaiting a prophet they expect there.
events.tie: Their descendants, Qaynuqa, Nadir and Qurayzah, would be the Prophet's ﷺ neighbours in Madinah.
events.note: When they came is uncertain. Reports range from the time of Musa to after 70 CE.

events.title: The owners of the garden
events.what: Brothers swear to harvest their garden at dawn so no poor person gets a share. Overnight it is burnt black, and they turn to Allah in regret.
events.note: Some early commentators place it at Darawan near Sana'a, after the time of Isa. Others treat it as a parable.

events.title: Sasanian Persia
events.what: The Sasanian dynasty takes Persia. For four centuries Persia and Rome fight over Iraq and Syria.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the reign of the Sasanian king Khosrau I, and his letter inviting Khosrau II to Islam was torn up.

events.title: The People of the Cave
events.what: Young believers flee a pagan king and sleep in a cave for 309 years. Where exactly is debated; Ephesus is the oldest claim.

events.title: The Classic Maya
events.what: Maya city-states like Tikal raise pyramids, write in glyphs and track the sun, moon and Venus with great precision.
events.tie: The Quran says: 'The sun and the moon move by precise calculation' (55:5).

events.title: Idols come to Makkah
events.what: Amr ibn Luhayy, chief of Makkah, brings idols from Syria and sets them around the Kaaba. The faith of Ibrahim is buried under idol worship.
events.note: The Prophet ﷺ said he saw him in the Fire; he was the first to set camels loose for the idols. His date is uncertain.

events.title: An emperor captured
events.what: The Persian king Shapur I defeats and captures the Roman emperor Valerian near Edessa. Rome and Persia stay at war for centuries.
events.tie: Surah al-Rum (30:2-4) would later foretell a turn in this same long war.

events.title: The Ghana empire
events.what: In West Africa, the Soninke build the empire of Ghana on gold from the south and salt from the Sahara.
events.tie: Muslim traders later crossed the Sahara to its capital, and the geographer al-Bakri described it in 1068.
events.note: Its beginnings are uncertain; some date them centuries later.

events.title: The Council of Nicaea
events.what: Constantine gathers bishops at Nicaea. They declare Isa 'of one substance' with God and condemn Arius, who taught that he was created.
events.tie: The Quran answers that Isa was a messenger of Allah and His word to Maryam: 'do not say three' (4:171).

events.title: The Namara inscription
events.what: On a tomb in the Syrian desert, an epitaph for Imru' al-Qays, 'king of all the Arabs', is carved in Arabic words with Nabataean letters.
events.tie: It is one of the oldest Arabic texts, three centuries before the Quran made Arabic a world language.

events.title: Constantinople
events.what: Constantine founds a new capital and makes Christianity the faith of the empire. Rome becomes Byzantium.
events.tie: Constantine's Council of Nicaea set the creed that Isa was divine; the Quran has Isa say he taught only 'worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord' (5:117).

events.title: Christian Abyssinia
events.what: The kingdom of Aksum in Abyssinia adopts Christianity. Its later king, the Najashi, shelters the first Muslim refugees.
events.tie: When the first Muslims fled there in 615, the Najashi wept at Surah Maryam and refused to hand them back to Quraysh.

events.title: One lawful faith
events.what: Emperor Theodosius makes Nicene Christianity the religion of the empire. Within twelve years pagan worship is banned.
events.tie: The Quran says: 'There shall be no compulsion in religion' (2:256).

events.title: Tubba of Himyar
events.what: A Himyarite king remembered as Tubba marches north, spares Yathrib and is said to be the first to clothe the Kaaba. The Quran names his people among nations destroyed.
events.note: Most identify him with As'ad Abu Karib, about 400 CE. A narration in Ahmad says 'Do not curse Tubba, for he became Muslim'; its strength is debated.

events.title: Qusayy gathers Quraysh
events.what: Qusayy ibn Kilab gathers the scattered clans of Quraysh in Makkah, takes the keys of the Kaaba and builds Dar al-Nadwah, the house of council.

events.title: Western Rome falls
events.what: The last western Roman emperor is deposed. Europe enters its early medieval age.
events.tie: Rome lived on in the east as Byzantium, the Rum of Surah ar-Rum (30:2), which the Muslims would later meet at Yarmuk.

events.title: Indian numerals
events.what: In Gupta India, Aryabhata writes his astronomy with place-value numbers. Indian mathematicians soon treat zero as a number.
events.tie: Al-Khwarizmi spread these numerals in Arabic, and Europe learned them as 'Arabic numerals'.

events.title: Winter and summer caravans
events.what: Hashim, great-grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ, makes pacts so Quraysh caravans travel safely to Yemen in winter and Syria in summer.

events.title: The People of the Ditch
events.what: A king in Yemen burns the believers of Najran in a fiery trench. Surah al-Buruj recalls the People of the Ditch.

events.title: Hagia Sophia
events.what: Justinian finishes the Hagia Sophia, the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years.
events.tie: Sultan Mehmed II made it a mosque in 1453; later sultans added minarets and great roundels bearing the names of Allah, the Prophet ﷺ and his companions.

events.title: Zamzam found again
events.what: Zamzam had been buried and lost for centuries. Told in a dream where to dig, Abd al-Muttalib uncovers the well and gives its water to the pilgrims.
events.note: From Ibn Ishaq's biography of the Prophet ﷺ.

events.title: The plague of Justinian
events.what: Bubonic plague sweeps the Mediterranean and kills a huge share of Constantinople. It returns again and again for two centuries.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ taught: if plague is in a land, do not enter it, and if you are in it, do not flee.

events.title: The dam of Saba breaks
events.what: The great dam of Saba breaks for the last time. Gardens turn to scrub and the tribes of Yemen scatter across Arabia.
events.tie: Tradition says tribes from Yemen, among them the Aws and Khazraj of Madinah, migrated north after the dam failed; they became the Ansar.

events.title: The Year of the Elephant
events.what: Abraha marches from Yemen with an elephant to destroy the Kaaba. Birds pelt his army with stones. The Year of the Elephant.
